1:1.headline: When the judges ruled, or when the judges were judged?
1:1.body: שפט השפטים reads simply as 'when the judges ruled'. Ibn Ezra brings a reading that God judged the judges, because the famine came through them.

sources.quote: יש אומר כי השם שפט השופטים, כי על ידם בא רעב בארץ ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a reading that God judged the judges, since the famine came because of them.

sources.quote: וחז"ל במליצתם אמרו אוי לדור ששפטו את שופטיהם
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages: woe to the generation that judged its judges.

1:2.headline: Ephrathites: people from Ephrat, or people of rank?
1:2.body: אפרתים can mean 'from Ephrat', an old name for Bethlehem. Rashi first reads it as 'important people' and explains it with a Greek word for well-born.

sources.quote: אֶבְגִּינוֹס. רְאֵה חֲשִׁיבוּתָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means important people, gives the Greek word for it, and also says Bethlehem was called Ephrat.

sources.quote: וזאת המלה פעם הוא ליחס המקום הנקרא אפרת, ופעם אחת ממשפחת אפרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word sometimes means from the place Ephrat and sometimes from the family of Ephraim.

sources.quote: הנה אפרת הוא בית לחם
sources.says: Ralbag says Ephrat is Bethlehem.

1:3.headline: Why call Elimelech 'Naomi's husband' just as he dies?
1:3.body: We already know whose husband he was. Rashi says it shows a man's death falls hardest on his wife, and that because he led the house, the judgment struck him and not her.

sources.quote: אֵין אִישׁ מֵת אֶלָּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says a man dies only to his wife, meaning she feels the loss most.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה אִישׁ נָעֳמִי וְשׁוֹלֵט עָלֶיהָ וְהִיא טְפֵלָה לוֹ, לָכֵן, פָּגְעָה בוֹ מִדַּת הַדִּין וְלֹא בָהּ
sources.says: Rashi adds that since he ruled over Naomi and she followed him, judgment struck him and not her.

sources.quote: לא נודע בשם רק שהיה איש נעמי שהיא נודעה שם יותר ממנו
sources.says: Malbim says that after he lost his wealth abroad, he was known only as Naomi's husband.

1:5.headline: 'They also died': first their wealth, then the sons
1:5.body: The small word גם, 'also', seems extra. Rashi says it hints that first their money and animals were lost, and only then did the sons die too.

sources.quote: בַּתְּחִלָּה לָקוּ בְמָמוֹנָם וּמֵתוּ גְמַלֵּיהֶם וּמִקְנֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says that first they were struck in their money and their camels and cattle died.

sources.quote: שתחלה ירד ממונם לטמיון ואח"כ מתו כי אין בעה"ר פוגע בנפשות תחלה
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages: first their money was lost, then they died, since the Merciful One does not strike lives first.

1:6.headline: She 'returned' while still in Moab: a return in her mind
1:6.body: The verse says Naomi returned before she has even set out. Ibn Ezra and Malbim say it means she made up her mind to go back.

sources.quote: ותשב משדה מואב. במחשבת. כמו וילחם ישראל עם בלק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says she returned in thought, just as Israel 'fought' Balak only in intent.

sources.quote: שהיא גמרה כן בדעתה בעודה בשדי מואב
sources.says: Malbim says she decided this while still in the fields of Moab.

1:7.headline: Why say she left? A good person's leaving is felt
1:7.body: The last verse already said she returned, so 'she went out from the place' seems extra. Rashi says it teaches that when a righteous person leaves a town, its glory leaves too.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא מַגִּיד שֶׁיְּצִיאַת צַדִּיק מִן הַמָּקוֹם נִכֶּרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that a righteous person's leaving a place is noticed.

sources.quote: פָּנָה זִיוָהּ, פָּנָה הֲדָרָהּ, פָּנָה שִׁבְחָהּ שֶׁל עִיר
sources.says: Rashi says the town's shine, beauty and praise leave with her.

1:13.headline: An uncommon verb: תשברנה means 'wait in hope'
1:13.body: Naomi asks: will you wait for sons not yet born? Rashi and Malbim read שבר here as hoping, as in Psalm 146, 'whose hope is in the LORD his God'.

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּא לָהֶם תְּצַפֶּינָה עַד אֲשֶׁר יִגְדָּלוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'will you wait for them until they grow up?', and compares 'whose hope is in the LORD'.

sources.quote: גדר השבר הוא המקוה על דבר ברור שהסברא נותנת שימלא תקותו בעתו
sources.says: Malbim says this word means hoping for something one has good reason to expect in time.

1:13.headline: A one-time word: shut in, like a man inside a circle
1:13.body: תעגנה appears only here. Rashi reads it as 'shut in', like 'he drew a circle and stood inside it', and rejects reading it as עיגון, being left bound.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן אָסוּר וְכָלוּא כְּמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means tied up and shut in, like one who drew a circle and stood in it.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין לְשׁוֹן עִגּוּן, וְלֹא יִתָּכֵן
sources.says: Rashi says some explain it as עיגון, but that cannot be right because of how it is spelled.

sources.quote: תעגנה. מבנין נפעל ואין לו חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this verb form has no other example.

1:13.headline: 'No, my daughters', or 'Woe, my daughters'?
1:13.body: Ibn Ezra reads אל as 'do not': do not come with me. Malbim cites a midrash that reads it as a cry of 'woe', as in 'wail like a maiden' in Joel.

sources.quote: אל בנותי. כלומר אל תלכנה עמי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'do not go with me'.

sources.quote: אל בנותי במדרש מפרש מלת אל, מלשון אלי כבתולה
sources.says: Malbim says the midrash reads אל as a lament, 'woe is me more than you'.

1:13.headline: God's hand 'went out' against her: every blow already spent
1:13.body: Elsewhere God's striking hand 'is' against someone. Malbim says 'went out' is used for it only here, and means every blow has already landed on Naomi.

sources.quote: יד ה' המורה על המכה לא נמצא בלשון יציאה רק בלשון הויה
sources.says: Malbim says the hand of God as a blow is never found with the verb 'go out', only with 'be'.

sources.quote: ולשון יציאה הבא פה מורה שכבר כלה בה כל מכותיו
sources.says: Malbim says 'went out' shows God had already finished all his blows on her.

sources.quote: כי יצאה בי. גזירת השם שיצא מלפניו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a decree of God that went out from him.

1:13.headline: The 'hand of the LORD' means a blow, not a hand
1:13.body: Rashi brings Rabbi Levi: wherever the Bible says 'the hand of the LORD', it means a plague. Ibn Ezra says it means a blow, since people strike with the hand.

sources.quote: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי, כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "יַד ה'" מַכַּת דֶּבֶר הוּא
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Levi that 'the hand of the LORD' always means a plague.

sources.quote: יד ה'. מכה כי ביד היא בלשון בני אדם דבר הכתוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a blow, since a blow is by hand, and Scripture speaks in human terms.

1:15.headline: The stress tells 'she went back' from 'she is going back'
1:15.body: שבה can mean 'she returned' or 'she is returning'. Rashi says the accent on the first syllable marks it as past: Orpah has already gone back.

sources.quote: זֶה טַעְמוֹ לְמַעְלָה תַּחַת הַשִּׁי"ן לְפִי שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עָבַר
sources.says: Rashi says the accent sits on the ש because the word is in the past tense.

1:16.headline: פגע can mean strike, meet, or plead
1:16.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read Ruth's words as 'do not press me' with your pleas. Malbim notes the verb can also mean to strike, and cites a midrash that hears 'do not sin against me'.

sources.quote: אַל תִּפְגְּעִי בִי. אַל תִּפְצְרִי בִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'do not urge me'.

sources.quote: אל תפגעי בי. הטעם פיוס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means coaxing, as in 'plead for me with Ephron'.

sources.quote: כי פגיעה משמש על ג' דברים: הריגה ויפגע בו וימת, פגישה ופגע ביריחו, תחנונים ופגעו לי בעפרון
sources.says: Malbim says the verb has three uses: killing, meeting, and pleading.

1:19.headline: 'The two of them': Ruth now stands equal to Naomi
1:19.body: The word שתיהם, 'the two of them', seems extra. Rashi and Malbim say it shows that once Ruth chose to join the Jewish people, the verse counts her as Naomi's equal.

sources.quote: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתְנָה דַעְתָּהּ לְהִתְגַּיֵּר, הִשְׁוָה אוֹתָהּ הַכָּתוּב לְנָעֳמִי
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Abbahu: once she set her mind to convert, the verse made her equal to Naomi.

sources.quote: שמלת שתיהן מיותר ובא להורות על השווי
sources.says: Malbim says the word is extra and comes to show they were equal.

1:21.headline: 'Full' of what? Wealth and sons, or a child on the way
1:21.body: Naomi says she left full and came back empty. Rashi says full means rich and with sons, or that she was pregnant when she left.

sources.quote: מְלֵאָה הָלַכְתִּי. בְּעֹשֶׁר וּבָנִים. דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁהָיְתָה מְעֻבֶּרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says she was full of wealth and sons, or, in another view, pregnant.

sources.quote: מלאה. בנים וממון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says full means with sons and money.

2:1.headline: A 'known one': a relative, or a close friend?
2:1.body: The word is written מידע and read מודע, from 'to know'. Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as a relative, while Malbim says it means someone who loved them and knew them well, not a distant kinsman.

sources.quote: מוֹדַע. קָרוֹב. בֶּן אָחִיו שֶׁל אֱלִימֶלֶךְ הָיָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means a relative: Boaz was the son of Elimelech's brother.

sources.quote: מודע. קרוב ידוע, כמו ומודע לבינה תקרא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a known relative, as in 'call understanding your kin'.

sources.quote: אוהבה ומכירה היטב לא אח רחוק
sources.says: Malbim says it means one who loved her and knew her well, not a distant relative.

2:1.headline: The sages say Boaz was also the judge Ibzan
2:1.body: Ibn Ezra brings the sages' view that Boaz is Ibzan, who judged Israel in the book of Judges. Rashi says the same in his comment on Judges.

sources.quote: שהוא אבצן שהיה שופט את ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra brings the sages' teaching that Boaz is Ibzan, who judged Israel.

sources.quote: אִבְצָן. זֶה בֹּעַז
sources.says: Rashi says Ibzan is Boaz.

2:7.headline: Gathering 'among the sheaves': forgotten sheaves, or her own bundles?
2:7.body: Rashi reads Ruth's request as asking for the sheaves the reapers forgot, which the Torah leaves to the poor. Malbim says she took only loose stalks and tied them into bundles herself, so no one would think she stole a sheaf.

sources.quote: וְאָסַפְתִּי בָעֳמָרִים. שִׁכְחָה שֶׁל עֳמָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says she meant the forgotten sheaves.

sources.quote: שכל מה שאספה בכדי עומר עשתה ממנו עומר, ולא תאמר שגנבה עומר מן העמרים של השדה
sources.says: Malbim says whatever she gathered that came to a sheaf's worth she made into a sheaf, so one should not think she stole from the field's sheaves.

2:14.headline: 'Come here', to a place above her station
2:14.body: Boaz tells Ruth גשי הלם, come here, to sit near him at the head of the meal. Malbim says הלום always marks a place higher than one's rank, and recalls the sages' saying that הלום means kingship.

sources.quote: ומלת הלום מציין תמיד מקום נעלה ממדרגתו
sources.says: Malbim says the word הלום always marks a place higher than the person's rank.

sources.quote: אין הלום אלא מלכות
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages: הלום means nothing but kingship.

2:16.headline: Drop stalks for her: 'pretend to forget', or 'let them fall'?
2:16.body: Boaz tells his men של תשלו לה. Rashi reads it as 'act as if you forgot', from the Aramaic word for an error, or as 'let fall', like olives dropping. Ibn Ezra adds a third reading from שלל, spoil.

sources.quote: שָׁכוֹחַ תִּשְׁכְּחוּ, עֲשׂוּ עַצְמֵיכֶם כְּאִלּוּ אַתֶּם שׁוֹכְחִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means forget on purpose: act as though you are forgetting.

sources.quote: כִּי יִשַּׁל זֵיתֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading, from 'your olives will drop'.

sources.quote: של תשלו. מגזרת שלל. ויש אומרים כמו שגגה מן על השל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from שלל, spoil, and that some read it as 'error'.

2:17.headline: An ephah of barley: a hidden code, or just the amount?
2:17.body: Ibn Ezra was asked what the ephah of barley means and answered that the verse just tells what happened. The man came back with number codes and prophecies he found in the words, and Ibn Ezra records them as the man's ideas. Ralbag simply gives the size: an ephah is three seahs.

sources.quote: אמרתי לו, אין טעם לשאלה הזאת, כי הכתוב ספר מה היה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he told the man the question has no point, because the verse is telling what happened.

sources.quote: שראתה רות בדרך נבואה כי עתיד היה אחד מבניה להעמיד עמוד על שם בעלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the man's first reading: Ruth saw by prophecy that a descendant would set up a pillar in her husband's name.

sources.quote: ויהי כאיפה שעורים. הנה האיפה שלש סאין
sources.says: Ralbag says an ephah is three seahs.

2:20.headline: How is Boaz kind to the dead?
2:20.body: Naomi blesses Boaz, who has not stopped his kindness to the living or the dead. Rashi says he feeds the living and took care of the needs of the dead. Malbim says the kindness to the dead is still ahead: marrying the widow to keep the dead man's name alive.

sources.quote: שֶׁזָּן וּמְפַרְנֵס אֶת הַחַיִּים וְנִטְפָּל בְּצָרְכֵי הַמֵּתִים
sources.says: Rashi says he feeds and supports the living and attended to the needs of the dead.

sources.quote: שבזה יעשה טובה לנפש המת
sources.says: Malbim says Naomi understood he would do good for the soul of the dead through levirate marriage.

2:20.headline: 'One of our redeemers': must he also marry Ruth?
2:20.body: A גואל is a close relative with the duty to redeem. Malbim says the redeemer must also marry the widow, to save the dead man's name, and that 'one of' hints there is another redeemer. Ibn Ezra says redeeming is not the same as levirate marriage.

sources.quote: והגואל צריך הוא ליבם שבזה יגאל נפש המת לבל ימחה שמו מישראל
sources.says: Malbim says the redeemer must marry the widow, which redeems the dead man so his name is not erased from Israel.

sources.quote: ואמרה מגואלנו הוא כי יש עוד גואל והוא אחד מהם
sources.says: Malbim says she said 'one of our redeemers' because there is another redeemer and Boaz is one of them.

sources.quote: מגואלנו הוא. אין הגאולה יבום רק הוא דרך אחרת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says redemption is not levirate marriage but something else.

3:3.headline: Written I will go down: Naomi's merit goes with Ruth
3:3.body: The word is read you will go down, but it is written I will go down. Rashi says the spelling hints that Naomi's merit will go down with Ruth.

sources.quote: וְיָרַדְתִּי כְּתִיב זְכוּתִי תֵרֵד עִמָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it is written I will go down, meaning my merit will go down with you.

3:4.headline: His feet, or the place at his feet?
3:4.body: Ibn Ezra says מרגלותיו simply means his feet, as in Daniel, and rejects the view that it is a cushion placed under the feet. Ralbag reads it as the end of the bed where the feet lie.

sources.quote: מרגלותיו. כמו רגליו וכן בדניאל. על כן טעה המפרש כי הוא כסת יושם תחת הרגלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means his feet, and whoever explained it as a cushion under the feet was mistaken.

sources.quote: הוא החלק מהמטה אשר הוא לפאת הרגלים
sources.says: Ralbag says it is the part of the bed at the side of the feet.

3:4.headline: Uncovering his feet as a silent hint about the shoe
3:4.body: Malbim says Naomi and Ruth were too shy to ask Boaz outright, so Ruth hinted by uncovering his feet. Bare feet recall the shoe ceremony for a man who refuses to marry his dead relative's widow, so the hint said: refuse and go barefoot, or lie beside me and raise a name for the dead.

sources.quote: כי הם בושו מלתבוע את בועז בפה שישא אותה
sources.says: Malbim says they were ashamed to ask Boaz aloud to marry her, so they used signs.

sources.quote: או תגלה רגליך להיות בלא נעל ותקרא בית חלוץ הנעל, או שאשכב בצדך להקים לקרובך שם בישראל
sources.says: Malbim says the hint was: either bare your feet and be called the house of the removed shoe, or let me lie beside you to raise a name for your relative.

3:7.headline: Boaz's glad heart: Rashi says he studied Torah
3:7.body: After eating and drinking, Boaz's heart was glad. Rashi reads the gladness as Boaz turning to study Torah.

sources.quote: וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ. עָסַק בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says his heart was glad means he occupied himself with Torah.

3:9.headline: Spread your wing: a cloak's corner, a bird's wing, shelter
3:9.body: כנף means a wing and also the corner of a garment. Rashi reads it as covering Ruth with Boaz's cloak, a way of speaking about marriage; Malbim hears a bird spreading its wings over its mate; and Maimonides reads it as spread your shelter over your servant.

sources.quote: כְּנַף בִּגְדְּךָ לְכַסּוֹתִי בְטַלִּיתְךָ וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן נִשּׂוּאִין
sources.says: Rashi says it means the corner of your garment, to cover me with your cloak, and it is language of marriage.

sources.quote: היא מליצה נלקחה מן העופות שפורשים כנפיהם על בני זוגם
sources.says: Malbim says it is an image taken from birds that spread their wings over their mates.

sources.quote: פירושו לדעתי: פרוש את סתרך־חסותך על שפחתך
sources.says: Maimonides says that in his view it means spread your cover and protection over your maidservant.

3:12.headline: A word that is written but not read aloud
3:12.body: The written text has אם, if, but it is not read aloud. Rashi notes that the word makes the sentence sound doubtful, while in fact it is certain that a closer redeemer exists.

sources.quote: אִם כְּתִיב וְלֹא קְרִי
sources.says: Rashi says אם is written but not read.

sources.quote: מַשְׁמַע סָפֵק וְהוּא וַדַּאי
sources.says: Rashi says the wording sounds like doubt, but the matter is certain.

3:16.headline: Who are you, or what happened to you?
3:16.body: Naomi surely knew Ruth, so why ask who she is? Malbim says it was still too dark to see, while Rabbi Yonah, quoted by Ibn Ezra, reads מי here as מה, meaning what happened to you.

sources.quote: מבואר שגם כשבאה לבית חמותה היה בטרם יכיר איש את רעהו ולכן שאלה מי הוא הבא
sources.says: Malbim says it was still before people could recognize each other, so Naomi asked who had come.

sources.quote: ויאמר רבי יונה המדקדק, כי 'מי' - 'מה'. והטעם 'מה היה לך'
sources.says: Ibn Ezra quotes Rabbi Yonah that מי here means מה: what happened to you.

3:18.headline: Why a matter falls: decisions come down from heaven
3:18.body: Naomi tells Ruth to wait and see how the matter will fall. Ibn Ezra explains the word: every decree comes down from heaven, so a matter is said to fall.

sources.quote: בעבור שכל הגזירות באות מן השמים, על כן יפול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it says fall because all decrees come from heaven.
